target_problem: constructive avoidance on the exact V101 residual signed-majority and mux/bijunctive frontier
conditional_implication: If a locality-three circuit has a strong affine backdoor B of size beta, exact output-prefix preimage counts are computable by enumerating 2^beta backdoor assignments and applying Gaussian elimination on each affine restriction. Greedy child minimization constructs a missing output in O(2^beta poly(N)). A size-k backdoor is detectable in O(3^k poly(N)) for arity at most three.

bridge_lemmas.name: strong affine backdoor makes every restricted output-prefix fiber an affine linear system
prefix preimage counts are exact sums over disjoint backdoor assignments
minimum-child prefix construction reaches zero preimages when m>n
locality-three strong affine backdoor detection is FPT by a <=3-way bounded search tree
every 0x1b mask has a unique one-variable selector backdoor
exact-stretch pure-0x1b family has beta=1 while V97 lambda=n, V100 zero peels, V101 mu=n
all residual 0x17/0x1b circuits have beta=O(log N)

current_gap: The strong affine backdoor number beta can be Theta(n). V102 gives no worst-case upper bound for arbitrary signed-majority/mux mixtures and therefore no unrestricted runtime improvement.
stop_rule: Do not promote V103 from another backdoor census. Require a structural beta upper bound/approximation with consequences, a hybrid functional-anchor plus affine-backdoor compression theorem, or an explicit lambda=mu=beta=Theta(n) obstruction followed by a new shrinking invariant.
external_validation_target: prior-art review of strong affine CSP backdoors specialized to range avoidance; comparison with Kuntewar-Sarma majority algorithms and Huang-Li-Zhong local algorithms
